subject: english-studies
title: Naming words (nouns)
summary: Find the words that name people, animals, places and things.

lesson.text: Some words are names. They tell us who or what we are talking about. We call them naming words, or nouns.

items: People: mother, teacher, doctor, Amina, Chidi

lesson.text: Ask: is this the name of a person, an animal, a place or a thing? If yes, it is a naming word.

lesson.title: The goat ate the yam.
steps: Is "goat" a name? Yes, it names an animal.
Is "ate" a name? No, it tells us what the goat did.
Is "yam" a name? Yes, it names a thing.
So the naming words are "goat" and "yam".

lesson.text: Special names start with a capital letter
The name of one particular person or place starts with a capital letter: Tunde, Kano, Nigeria. A general name does not: boy, city, country.
Practise at home: point at things around you and say their names. Every one of them is a naming word.

questions.prompt: Which word is a naming word?
questions.explanation: "Book" names a thing. "Run" is something you do, "happy" describes how you feel and "quickly" describes how something is done.

questions.prompt: In "Ngozi went to the market", which word names a place?
questions.explanation: "Market" is a place. "Ngozi" is also a naming word, but it names a person.

questions.prompt: Which naming word should start with a capital letter?
questions.explanation: Abuja is the name of one particular city, so it is written with a capital letter: Abuja.

questions.prompt: Which of these names an animal?
questions.explanation: A hen is an animal. A farm is a place, a spoon is a thing and a nurse is a person.
